coverageText: 9.9 tiles/m² at 75mm headlap, 10.7 tiles/m² at 100mm headlap
notes: Popular flat interlocking concrete tile with slate-like appearance. Broken bond laying pattern.
Classic concrete plain tile, 12mm thick. Available in multiple colours.

coverageText: 9.7 tiles/m² at 75mm headlap, 10.5 tiles/m² at 100mm headlap
notes: Thin 18mm leading edge — 40% thinner than standard interlocking tiles. Slate-like appearance.
Small format interlocking tile, popular for re-roofing. Less wastage due to smaller size.
Classic double Roman profile, iconic on UK roofs. Traditional appearance.
13mm thick cross-cambered concrete plain tile. Available in 11 finishes.
Classic clay plain tile in production since 1837. 13mm thick. Available in 8 colours.
Economical interlocking concrete tile, used on UK roofs for over 50 years. Similar to Sandtoft Standard Pattern and Marley Ludlow Plus.

coverageText: 22.7 tiles/m² at 100mm headlap, 20.5 tiles/m² at 75mm headlap
notes: Humber clay interlocking plain tile. Low pitch performance down to 15°. Broken bond only.
Classic 15" x 9" concrete interlocking tile. One of the most widely used tiles in the UK. Similar to Redland 49 and Marley Ludlow Plus.

coverageText: 9.7 tiles/m² at 75mm headlap, 10.4 tiles/m² at 100mm headlap
notes: Large format low pitch tile with clean minimalist lines. 29mm thick. Ideal for extensions and low pitch roofs.
Double pantile profile with elegant flowing lines. Mendip 12.5 variant can go as low as 12.5°.
Machine made natural clay plain tile. 11mm thick. Market leading 30° minimum pitch. Available in 11 colours.

coverageText: 10.5 tiles/m² at 318mm gauge, 9.7 tiles/m² at 343mm gauge
notes: High bold roll profile — striking wavy effect. Very low minimum pitch of 12.5°, ideal for extensions and lean-to roofs.

coverageText: 10.5 tiles/m² at 318mm gauge, 9.7 tiles/m² at 343mm gauge
notes: Double pantile profile with gentle flowing lines. Faster and easier to lay than traditional single pantiles.

coverageText: 10.5 tiles/m² at 318mm gauge, 9.7 tiles/m² at 343mm gauge
notes: Large format low profile concrete interlocking tile. 26mm thick. Neat square-edged profile. Larger version of the Redland 49.

coverageText: 10.7 slates/m² at 318mm gauge, 9.9 slates/m² at 343mm gauge
notes: Economical concrete slate. 31mm thick. Must be laid broken bond. 60 year life expectancy.
Discontinued tile (made 1960s-1999). Large format concrete interlocking tile. Often seen alongside Stonewold.
Concrete slate effect tile with 30% reduction in embodied carbon. Hanging length 396mm.
Double camber interlocking plain tile. 15mm thick. 40% reduction in CO2 vs traditional tiles. Available in 12 colours.
Very low pitch tile — down to 12.5°. Popular for garages and extensions. Available in autumn, slate grey, red and brown.
Through-coloured concrete plain tile. Two nail holes. Improved air circulation design.

coverageText: 60 tiles/m² at 100mm gauge, 53 tiles/m² at 115mm gauge
notes: 200-year heritage Etruria Marl clay tile from Staffordshire. Natural colours from kiln atmosphere — no artificial stains. Tested to 400+ freeze-thaw cycles.
Heather blue/purple natural Welsh slate from Penrhyn Quarry, Snowdonia. 100 year guarantee. Three grades: Capital (5.5mm), County (7mm), Celtic (9mm).
Heather blue/purple natural Welsh slate. Medium format. 100 year guarantee.
Small format Penrhyn heather blue Welsh slate. Used for intricate details and small roofs.
Blue-grey natural Welsh slate with smooth riven texture. From Ffestiniog Quarry, in production since 1818. 100 year guarantee.
Medium format Ffestiniog blue-grey Welsh slate. Smooth riven texture, elegant appearance.
Humber clay plain tile from Sandtoft. Traditional plain tile profile.
Traditional clay S-curve pantile. Easy to fit with open gauge design and thin leading edge.
Traditionally handcrafted clay plain tile. Unique mellow appearance and granular texture. Each tile has natural irregularities.
Made from over 60% recycled slate. Minimum pitch 15°. Natural slate appearance with proven durability.

coverageText: 9.8 tiles/m² at 75mm headlap, 10.6 tiles/m² at 100mm headlap
notes: Large format interlocking tile with classic square profile. 25mm thick. Made from ~50% recycled materials. Popular for refurbishments.
Deep rolled interlocking profile with strongly undulating surface. Mediterranean pantile look. Now discontinued — widely seen on UK roofs.
Classic double Roman profile — graceful roll and subtle pans. 51mm thick. Available in 9 colours.

coverageText: 17.8 tiles/m² at 281mm gauge, 16.3 tiles/m² at 306mm gauge
notes: Replaced the Norfolk Pantile. Classic single pantile shape in modern interlocking concrete. 24mm thick. Characteristic of South East and East Anglia.
Discontinued large format flat profile concrete interlocking slate. NOT interchangeable with Mk1. Very widely used on UK roofs 1970s-2000s.
Classic pantile proportions in interlocking concrete. Same size as traditional clay pantiles. Available in 5 smooth and 2 sandfaced finishes.
Large format interlocking concrete pantile. Low minimum pitch of 15° with 100mm headlap.
Traditional clay pantile with S-curve profile. Available in Antique Slate, Flanders, Tuscan and Natural Red.
Cost-effective concrete slate-appearance tile with interlocking design. Dual Calderdale variant has central groove for small-format slate appearance.
Most common UK slate size — accounts for ~80% of English/Welsh slate use. Dark grey/blue-black. 4-5mm thick. Quarried in north-west Spain. BS EN 12326 compliant.
Larger format — better performance in high exposure areas and shallower pitches. Common in London, Manchester and surrounding areas. Holed at 115mm as standard.
Common in Scotland and northern England. Similar to the 16x10 imperial size previously from Welsh quarries. 4-5mm thick.
Smaller format used in northern regions. Known as 'Lady' in traditional imperial sizing. 4-5mm thick.
Wider format for better coverage in high rainfall areas. 4-5mm thick Spanish natural slate.
Dark grey/blue-black natural slate. 4-6mm thick. Pre-holed, chamfered edges. Complies with BS EN 12326-1:2014 S1, W1, T1. Cost-effective alternative to Welsh/Spanish slate.
Smaller format Chinese natural slate. 4-6mm thick. Dark grey colour. BS EN 12326 compliant.
Large format Chinese natural slate. 4-6mm thick. Good for shallow pitches and high exposure areas.
Iconic double Roman profile — seen on UK roofs for 2000 years. Modern concrete interlocking version. Smooth finish available.
Concrete plain tile with natural weathering appearance combining clay look with machine-made durability.
Dark blue-grey Welsh slate from Cwt-y-Bugail quarry, Blaenau Ffestiniog. Distinctive banding (relic bedding). Formed from Ordovician slate beds 470 million years ago. 100 year guarantee.
Medium format dark blue-grey Welsh natural slate. Three grades: Capital (5.5mm), County (7mm), Celtic (9mm).
Edgemere with randomised riven texture — closely resembles natural slate. 18mm thin leading edge. 40% thinner than standard interlocking tiles.
Lightweight interlocking slate made from over 80% recycled natural slate waste. Labour efficient.
Ultra low pitch variant of Mendip — minimum 12.5°. Ideal for single storey extensions and refurbishments. Same appearance as standard Mendip on the roof.
Redland's Landmark range Double Roman profile. Classic interlocking double Roman concrete tile.
10 slates/m² with unique single annular ring-shank fixing. Thin leading edge. MockBond variant has central bond line giving appearance of two smaller slates.
